text:
MIAMI, June 18, 2025
The new era of Real Madrid , under coach Chabi Alonso, began with a 1-1 draw against Saudi Al-Hilal in the first round of the World Club Championship group stage at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami. The other teams in Group H are Pachuca and Salzburg. The match was a thrilling, back-and-forth battle that left fans on the edge of their seats.
The game was a debut for Alonso and Simone Inzagi near the touchline. Also making their debuts for Real Madrid were Trent Alexander-Arnold and Dean Hususen. Young Gonzalo Garcia scored in the 34th minute, giving Real Madrid the lead. Al-Hilal equalized in the 41st minute with a penalty kick from Ruben Nevesh. In the added time, Bono saved a penalty from Fede Valverde.
al-hilal had the first significant chance of the match. Sergei Milinkovic-Savic unleashed a powerful shot from outside the penalty area, but Tibo Courtois made the save. Moments later, Federico Valverde fouled Milinkovic-Savic, resulting in a free kick, but the shot was blocked by the wall.
Just 2 minutes of @Alhilal_en turning on the HEAT against @realmadrid ????

– DAZN Football (@DAZNFootball) June 18, 2025
In the sixth minute, Raul Assensio, the central defender for Real Madrid, attempted a long-range shot that Yasin Bono saved without difficulty.
In the tenth minute, Al-Hilal created another excellent opportunity. Salem Al-Dausari’s shot was off target, but Marcos Leonardo managed too redirect the ball towards the right corner, although it narrowly missed Courtois’s goal.
9′ UUUH SO CLOSE! @Alhilal_en putting real pressure and almost open the score ????
Watch the @Fifacwc | june 14 – July 13 | Every Game | Free | https://t.co/i0K4eUtwwb | #Fifacwc #The cooktheworld #RMahil pic.twitter.com/J4gHzdXv0E
– DAZN Football (@DAZNFootball) June 18, 2025
Real Madrid took the lead in the 34th minute. After a cross from the right, Gonzalo Garcia found himself in the right place at the right time and scored with a precise shot, making it 1:0.
Al-Hilal equalized in the 41st minute through a penalty. Dean Hususen fouled Marcos Leonardo in the penalty area, and the referee pointed to the spot. Ruben Nevesh confidently converted the penalty, leveling the score at 1:1.
real Madrid had a near miss seconds into the second half. Vinisius broke through on the left flank and found Arda Guler in the penalty area, but the shot hit the crossbar. A new center from Vinnie followed to Guler, but Bono saved the header.
46′ What a restart! @realmadrid almost hit the net within seconds of the second half! ????
Watch the @Fifacwc | June 14 – July 13 | Every Game | Free | https://t.co/i0K4eUtwwb | #fifacwc #The cooktheworld #RMahil pic.twitter.com/WrmD6j7xbn
– DAZN football (@DAZNFootball) June 18, 2025
In the 51st minute, Real Madrid captain Federico Valverde attempted a long-range shot that went wide. Two minutes later, Al-Hilal responded, with Dean Hususen making a mistake, allowing Marcos Leonardo to shoot, but the shot was to the side.
Real Madrid was a bit more active in the second half. In the 67th minute,Arda Gueller’s shot went wide. In the 72nd minute, Salem al-Dausari made a good run on the left, finding Marcos Leonardo in the penalty area, but the Brazilian’s shot went over the goal. A minute later, Bono saved Valverde’s shot.
Missed Penalty and Final Moments In added time, Real Madrid was awarded a penalty after Mohammed al-Kachtani fouled Fran Garcia. Fede Valverde took the penalty, but Yasin Bono saved it, preventing Real Madrid from taking the lead.
90+1′ THIS IS INSANE! Penalty to @realmadrid Valverde from the spot and Bono SAVES IT! We are still level in Miami! ????
Watch the @Fifacwc | June 14 – july 13 | Every Game | Free | https://t.co/i0K4eUtwwb | #Fifacwc #The cooktheworld #RMahil pic.twitter.com/CpwOek3yWy
– DAZN Football (@DAZNFootball) June 18, 2025
In the closing stages, Gonzalo garcia could have been the hero after a header, but Yasin Bono saved.Oreshian saucepes also headed the ball from a corner, but it went over the goal.
The game ended with both teams earning one point.

MIAMI, June 18, 2025
The new era of Real Madrid , under coach Chabi Alonso, began with a 1-1 draw against Saudi Al-hilal in the first round of the World Club Championship group stage at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami. The other teams in Group H are Pachuca and Salzburg. The match was a thrilling, back-and-forth battle that left fans on the edge of their seats.
The game was a debut for Alonso and simone Inzagi near the touchline. Also making their debuts for Real Madrid were trent Alexander-Arnold and Dean Hususen. Young Gonzalo Garcia scored in the 34th minute, giving real Madrid the lead. Al-Hilal equalized in the 41st minute with a penalty kick from Ruben Nevesh.In the added time,Bono saved a penalty from Fede Valverde.
Here’s a closer look at some of the key tactical battles and individual performances that shaped the encounter between Real Madrid and Al-Hilal:
Tactical Battles Real Madrid’s Midfield Dominance: coach Chabi Alonso set up Real Madrid with a midfield that aimed to control possession and dictate the tempo. The trio of Federico Valverde, jude Bellingham, and Rodrigo provided both defensive solidity and creative spark. Their ability to win the ball back quickly and transition into attack was crucial. however, against Al-Hilal’s compact defense, the midfield sometimes struggled to unlock the final third.
Al-Hilal’s Defensive Setup: Simone Indzagi opted for a defensive approach, focusing on a well-organized backline and rapid counter-attacks.The defensive unit, led by Hassan Al Tambakti and Kalidou Koulibaly, did a commendable job in containing Real Madrid’s attacking threats. They were especially effective in stifling the movement of Vinicius and Arda Guler, forcing Real Madrid to rely on crosses and long-range shots.
Set-piece Strategies: Both teams showed the importance of set pieces during the match. Real Madrid capitalized on a cross to score their goal,while Al-Hilal earned their equalizer from the spot. The final minutes saw numerous throws and corners from both sides. The missed penalty by Valverde and the save by Bono highlighted the importance of converting these critical moments.
Key Player Performances Yasin Bono (Al-Hilal): The moroccan goalkeeper was arguably the standout player of the match. Bono made crucial saves throughout the game, including a penalty save in added time, which ultimately earned Al-Hilal a valuable point. His command of the box and shot-stopping abilities were critical in frustrating Real Madrid’s attackers.
Marcos Leonardo (Al-Hilal): The Brazilian forward showed flashes of brilliance with his pace and trickery. He was a constant threat to Real Madrid’s defense, drawing the penalty for Al-Hilal’s equalizer. Although he did not score, his movement and ability to link up with his teammates created numerous opportunities.
Federico Valverde (Real Madrid): The Real Madrid captain was a dynamic presence in midfield, driving forward from deep positions.Despite the missed penalty, his energy and ability to win the ball back in key areas were vital for real Madrid’s performance.
Gonzalo Garcia (Real Madrid): The young forward demonstrated the opportunism needed to score. His goal,however,was the highlight of his game. Garcia’s ability to be in the right place at the right time, providing a cool finish to give Real Madrid the lead demonstrated his potential.
Looking Ahead The draw between Real Madrid and Al-Hilal sets the stage for an intriguing Group H. Real Madrid will need to sharpen their attack and improve their finishing to secure victories in upcoming matches against Pachuca and Salzburg. Al-Hilal, with their resolute defense and counter-attacking threat, will look to build on this positive result and upset their opponents.
